title: Getting Started with Burn
excerpt: Learn how to build and train your first neural network using Burn, the Rust deep learning framework designed for performance and flexibility.
body_md:
# Getting Started with Burn

Burn is a comprehensive deep learning framework built in Rust that prioritizes flexibility, performance, and ease of use.

## Installation

Add Burn to your `Cargo.toml`:

```toml
[dependencies]
burn = "0.14"
burn-ndarray = "0.14"
```

## Your First Model

```rust
use burn::prelude::*;
use burn::nn;

#[derive(Module, Debug)]
pub struct MnistModel<B: Backend> {
    linear1: nn::Linear<B>,
    linear2: nn::Linear<B>,
    activation: nn::Relu,
}
```

## Training Loop

Burn provides a built-in `Learner` that handles training with metrics, logging, and checkpointing out of the box.

## Next Steps

- Explore the Burn book for advanced topics
- Try different backends (wgpu, tch, candle)
- Build a real project with Burn

# Building an AI Agent with Rig

Rig is a Rust library for building LLM-powered applications with a focus on ergonomics and type safety.

## Setup

```toml
[dependencies]
rig-core = "0.6"
tokio = { version = "1", features = ["full"] }
```

## Creating a Simple Agent

```rust
use rig::providers::openai;

#[tokio::main]
async fn main() -> Result<(), anyhow::Error> {
    let client = openai::Client::from_env();
    
    let agent = client
        .agent("gpt-4")
        .preamble("You are a helpful Rust programming assistant.")
        .build();
    
    let response = agent.prompt("Explain ownership in Rust").await?;
    println!("{response}");
    Ok(())
}
```

## Adding Tools

Rig makes it easy to define tools that your agent can use during reasoning.

## RAG with Rig

Add vector search and document retrieval to ground your agent's responses in real data.
